problem.headline: You shouldn't spend your weekend editing.

pains.headline: Every minute of silence costs you two.
pains.body: A 10 minute video contains 3 to 4 minutes of silence, stumbles, and filler words, all cut manually, one by one.

pains.headline: One video. Four exports. Endless hours.
pains.body: The same video needs to be reformatted, re encoded, and re captioned for every platform, a process that can take as long as the original edit.
pains.bodyAccent: reformatted, re encoded, and re captioned
pains.bodyBold: as long as the original edit.

pains.headline: Pro tools are built for pros, not creators.
pains.body: Professional tools are powerful but designed for full time editors, not creators who edit as part of a larger job.
pains.bodyBold: as part of a larger job.

problem.kicker: The result: you either publish content that isn't as good as it could be, or spend your weekend editing.

q1.q: Do I need to know how to edit?
q1.a: No. The first pass runs on its own and gives you something playable. If you want a cut changed after that, you ask for it in words.

q2.q: How long does a pass take?
q2.a: Short edits usually come back in five to fifteen seconds. Longer recordings take proportionally more, and you can keep working while they run.

q3.a: Camera files, screen recordings and audio. The free plan takes videos up to twenty minutes, Creator up to ninety, Pro up to four hours.

q4.q: Can I still change things by hand?
q4.a: Yes. Every cut the pass makes is a normal cut you can move, trim or remove, and you can ask for changes in plain language instead.

q5.a: On EU infrastructure. Storage runs for seven days on the free plan, thirty on Creator, and for as long as you subscribe on Pro.

q6.q: What happens when the free passes run out?
q6.a: Editing by hand keeps working, including silence removal and trim. The AI passes come back next month, or straight away if you upgrade.
